body.p: By this response, claims 1, 3-17, and 19-22 are pending. Claims 1, 11, and 17 are amended. No new subject matter is added.
I. Examiner Interview

Applicant thanks the Examiners for their time on August 21, 2024 at 2:30 eastern to discuss the present case with Applicant's representative, Serene Sahar. Applicant's representative and the Examiners discussed the language of the independent claims and to try and determine an amendment that would help clarify the claims to distinguish over the prior art of record. In particular, the language relating to calculating a correction factor was discussed as well as a proposed amendment to clarify that the pilot input and the sensed force on the landing gear are inputs used to calculate the correction factor. A general agreement was reach, however, the Examiner will conduct further searching as standard practice requires.
II. Rejections Under 35 U.S.C. 4 102 and 103

Claims 1-3, 5, 11-14, and 17-19 are rejected are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) as being anticipated by Vallart et al. US 20160327958 ("Vallart"). Claims 4, 15, and 20 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Vallart in view of Romana et al. US 20170008619 ("Romana"). Claims 6-8 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Vallart in view of White EP 3208190 ("White"). Claims 9-10 and 16 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Vallart in view of Waltner et al. US 20180305038 ("Waltner").
a. Independent Claim 1

Amended independent claim 1 recites a control system for an aircraft including, among other things, a controller configured to receive the pilot input via the pilot input device, receive a sensed force on the landing gear via the first sensor, calculate an output command based at least on the pilot input and the force on the landing gear, wherein the controller calculates the output command by calculating a correction factor, wherein the pilot input and the sensed force on the landingz gear are inputs used to calculate the correction factor, and transmit the output command to control the aircraft.

The Examiner rejects independent claim 1 as being anticipated by Vallart. Claim 1 has been amended to provide further clarity on calculating the correction factor using the pilot input and the sensed force on the landing gear as inputs, as discussed during the Examiner interview.

Vallart fails to teach or suggest calculating a correction factor, wherein the pilot input and the sensed force on the landing gear are inputs used to calculate the correction factor. Rather, Vallart uses force sensors merely for the purpose of identifying whether the rotocraft is in an "in flight" state or a "touching" state. However, once the state of the rotocraft is identified, there is no indication that the information obtained from the sensors is used to calculate a correction factor. More specifically, Vallart discloses a control system for a rotocraft, which includes a means for detecting a ground reaction force F1, F2, F3 exerted on the landing gear for the purpose of identifying the state of the rotocraft between an "in flight" state and a "touching" state. Vallart [0038]-[0040]. The "touching" state is identified when the following two conditions are met: 1) the reaction force F1 is greater than the low threshold (SH) value but lower than the high threshold (SH) value; and 2) each of the reaction forces F2 and F3 is lower than the low threshold (Ss) value. Vallart [0041]-[0043]. The "in flight" state is identified when each of the reaction forces F1, F2, F3 is lower than the low threshold (Ss) value. Vallart [0044]. Once the controller determines which flight state the rotocraft is in, it is able to determine which control logic should be implemented. A first control law is implemented when the rotorcraft is in an "in flight" state, and a second control law is implemented when the rotocraft is in a "touching" state. Vallart [0046]-[0047]. In other words, the reaction forces F1, F2, F3 are used to determine which flight state the rotocraft is in, and thus, which control laws to use depending on the state.
Accordingly, Vallart discloses the use of sensors on the landing gear solely for the

purpose of determining a flight state of the rotocraft. However, Vallart fails to teach or suggest calculating a correction factor, wherein the pilot input and the sensed force on the landing gear are inputs used to calculate the correction factor.

None of the other cited references cure the deficiency of Vallart. Therefore, Applicant respectfully submits that claim 1 is allowable over the prior art. Claims 3-10 and 21-22 ultimately depend from claim 1 and are allowable for at least these reasons, in addition to independent reasons not discussed herein.
b. Independent Claim 11

Amended independent claim 11 recites a method of controlling an aircraft including, among other things, receiving a pilot input including a setpoint, receiving a first signal from a first sensor positioned on a landing gear of the aircraft, and calculating a first correction factor, wherein the setpoint and the first signal are inputs used to calculate the first correction factor.

The Examiner rejects independent claim 11 as being anticipated by Vallart. As explained in further detail above with respect to claim 1, Vallart fails to teach or suggest calculating a correction factor, wherein the setpoint and the first signal are inputs used to calculate the first correction factor. Rather, Vallart uses force sensors merely for the purpose of identifying whether the rotocraft is in an "in flight" state or a "touching" state. Accordingly, Vallart discloses the use of sensors on the landing gear solely for the purpose of determining a flight state of the rotocraft. However, Vallart fails to teach or suggest utilizing sensors on the landing gear to calculate a correction factor.

None of the other cited references cure the deficiency of Vallart. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that claim 11 is allowable over the prior art. Claims 12-16 ultimately depend from claim 11 and are allowable for at least these reasons, in addition to independent reasons not discussed herein.
c. Independent Claim 17

Amended independent claim 17 recites a control system for an aircraft including, among other things, a plurality of sensors positioned on a corresponding landing gear of the aircraft and configured to sense a parameter on the corresponding landing gear, and a configured to calculate an output command based on the pilot input and the sensed parameters of the landing gear, wherein the controller calculates the output command by calculating a correction factor, wherein the setpoint and the first signal are inputs used to calculate the first correction factor.

The Examiner rejects independent claim 17 as being anticipated by Vallart. As explained in further detail above with respect to claim 1, Vallart fails to teach or suggest calculating a correction factor, wherein the setpoint and the first signal are inputs used to calculate the first correction factor. Rather, Vallart uses force sensors merely for the purpose of identifying whether the rotocraft is in an "in flight" state or a "touching" state. Accordingly, Vallart discloses the use of sensors on the landing gear solely for the purpose of determining a flight
state of the rotocraft. However, Vallart fails to teach or suggest utilizing sensors on the landing gear to calculate a correction factor.

None of the other cited references cure the deficiency of Vallart. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that claim 17 is allowable over the prior art. Claims 19-20 ultimately depend from claim 17 and are allowable for at least these reasons, in addition to independent reasons not discussed herein.
d. Dependent Claims

As mentioned above, each of the dependent claims is patentable for individual reasons not specifically discussed herein. For the sake of brevity, Applicant has focused the present remarks on the independent claims. However, it should be noted that Applicant contends that the prior art does not teach, suggest, or render obvious any of the subject matter recited in dependent claims 3-10, 12-16, or 19-22.
III. Conclusion

In view of the amendments and remarks presented herein, it is respectfully submitted that the claims are in condition for allowance. Therefore, Applicant requests withdrawal of the present rejections and/or objections in order to allow the application to be allowed. Applicant requests that the Examiner telephone the attorneys or agents of record in the event a telephone discussion would be helpful in advancing the prosecution of this application.
